title: Exploring Sectoral Profitability in the Indian Stock Market Using Deep Learning

data_binding.reason: shared benchmark data replaces the paper's native dataset and protocol

paper_value.target: NSE Auto sector top-ten stocks, with sector-level averages reported
requirements: Daily stock price records for each selected NSE Auto sector stock from 2005-01-01 through 2024-04-23.
Input features reported as open, high, low, close, and volume for the model-design phase.
Use past 50 days of historical stock price records as the input window for each prediction.
Use the Auto sector top-ten NSE stocks and weights reported from the NSE report dated March 24, 2024.

dimensions.implication: The benchmark uses a frozen shared dataset rather than the paper's original data.
Only an explicitly named MethodCard model branch may enter the benchmark.

paper_value.preprocessing: The paper states that transformed and pre-processed data are provided to the model-processing function, but the exact transformations, scaler type, fit scope, missing-value handling, corporate-action adjustment, and train-only versus full-sample statistics are unknown.

dimensions.implication: Shared features isolate model behavior but do not reproduce the paper's end-to-end pipeline.

paper_value.evaluation: Evaluate on out-of-sample test data using Huber Loss, MAE, and Accuracy Score for next-day price-direction prediction. For profitability, simulate mandatory daily trading of a single equity share: buy if predicted next-day price is higher than current-day price, sell if predicted next-day price is lower than or equal to current-day price; profits are calculated using actual next-day prices. Exact chronological split and test-period boundaries for Table 20 are unknown.

dimensions.implication: The shared temporal split and metric definitions control comparability across methods.

dimensions.paper_value: Mandatory trading every day of a single equity share is assumed. Transaction costs, slippage, taxes, bid-ask spread, and financing costs are unknown.
dimensions.implication: Trading claims require matched cost and position rules; prediction-only metrics do not establish tradability.

paper_vs_run_delta.original_paper_hypothesis_reason: Shared benchmark data/features/splits differ from the native paper protocol; the original claim cannot be proved or disproved by this run.
paper_vs_run_delta.adapted_task_hypothesis_reason: The method beats the task-appropriate no-leakage baseline.
